title: ICA PolComm Summer School
text:
Sponsorship Details
satRday is committed to being an affordable and open conference for all interested R users. To provide highly discounted tickets, we plan to raise $10,000 with sponsors this year.
Sponsorship price is $1,000 and includes:

Three (3) individual registrations (a $50 value)
Your organization’s logo displayed on the conference website and at the beginning of each talk
An optional 5-minute slot at the conference where you may talk about how you use R in your organization

Sponsors will benefit from direct access to one of the main organizers to address any questions or extra requests.

title: About ICA Political Communication Summer School
text:
About ICA Political Communication Summer School




The Lectures
The School brings together world-reknowned researchers in political communication to address key theoretical and empirical questions as they arise around the globe. Through lectures, workshops, and small-group intensive feedback sessions, participants engage with cutting-edge research on the relationships between political communication, media, political participation, and democracy, while developing their own projects under the close mentorship of leading scholars in the field.


The Faculty
The 2026 Faculty gathers internationally renowned academics to engage with students. Confirmed in-person speakers include: Christian Baden (The Hebrew University of Jerusalem), Stephen Coleman (University of Leeds), Dam Hee Kim (Korea University), Regina Lawrence (University of Oregon), Joerg Matthes (University of Vienna), Patricia Moy (University of Washington), Chris Fei Shen (City University of Hong Kong), Lone Sorensen (University of Leeds), Talia Stroud (University of Texas at Austin), Sebastián Valenzuela (Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile), Claes de Vreese (University of Amsterdam).


The Students
Participants come from around the globe; countries represented at previous Summer Schools include Australia, Brazil, Canada, Colombia, the Czech Republic, Finland, France, Germany, India, Italy, Latvia, The Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, Pakistan, Poland, Portugal, Russia, Serbia, Slovakia, South Africa, Spain, Sweden, Turkey, UK, USA, among others.












A Successful Experience
Building on the experience of the last 15 years, the 2026 Summer School offers a unique opportunity for 30 PhD candidates and early career academics in communication, political science, sociology, and psychology:

to attend an immersive, five-day program that comprises lectures, master classes, paper presentations, and mentoring sessions, and
to build long-lasting personal and scholarly relations in a celebrated, friendly, and productive environment.

title: Application Details
text:
Application Details



The School addresses key theoretical and empirical questions in political communication, with faculty lectures focusing on democratic citizenship, democratic backsliding and resilience, AI, digital media and misinformation, civic engagement, and polarization. Students who are working on political communication questions in these areas are invited to apply. For themes in political communication covered by our division, see the ICA Political Communication Division homepage.
Building on the experience of the last 17 years, the 2026 Summer School offers a unique opportunity for PhD candidates and early-career academics in communication, sociology, psychology and political science:

to attend an immersive, five-day program that comprises lectures, master classes, paper presentations, and mentoring sessions, and
to build long-lasting personal and scholarly relations in a celebrated friendly and productive environment.

Participation will be on a competitive basis. Candidates interested in applying to the ICA Summer School should submit a three-page research proposal or an extended abstract of a research paper on issues broadly related to political communication. Submissions should include the name, email address, institutional affiliation, a brief bio (max. 200 words) mentioning main research interests and ongoing projects. A recommendation letter should be sent by a referee of your choice via email to cdp@leeds.ac.uk by March 25 at the latest. An international selection committee will review the applications.

Key Dates and Fees

Application Deadline: March 23 (23:59 UK time)
Recommendation Letter Submissions by Referees: March 25 (23:59 UK time)
Notifications of Acceptance: April 15
Enrollment fee: £550 (covers accommodation, daytime meals/catering, teaching programme, and Sunday night arrival).
